title: One block of derivative straightening and transport of exact projections
statement:
Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field and $B$ a smooth finite-type $k$-scheme with etale coordinates $(w,y)$ and distinguished point $a$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $T$ be previously formal transverse variables and $f_i=\sum_\gamma c_{i\gamma}(w,y)T^\gamma$ have regular coefficients on $B$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. At $a$ suppose their first exponents, for ascending total-degree lexicographic order with complementary variables first, are the minimal vertices $\alpha_i$ of a monotone diagram: $\alpha-\alpha_u e_u+\alpha_u e_v$ belongs to the diagram whenever $\alpha$ does and $u<v$. Order the vertices and group them by equal degree; $s_\ell$ is the last index of block $\ell$, and $Z^\ell$ is the set of variables occurring in its prefix. Assume $T=Z^{\ell-1}$, $y$ is precisely the newly essential block, and earlier stages are smooth closed coefficient schemes with their derivative equations and invertible transverse Jacobians. Fix $Q\ge\max_i|\alpha_i|-1$. For every earlier $h<\ell$ and $i>s_h$, assume the coefficients of $(Z^h)^\beta$ vanish identically as series in all other variables whenever $\beta$ lies in the prefix diagram restricted to $Z^h$ and $|\beta|\le Q$. Suppose the $f_i$ belong to, and generate, an ideal $K_b$ in each centered Taylor ring, with the identifications inherited from the earlier stages. Choose for each newly essential variable $j$ a vertex $\alpha_{i(j)}=\beta_j+e_j$ in its first block, with $\beta_j$ supported in $Z^\ell$; derivatives in $y$ are coordinate derivations and those in $T$ are formal derivatives [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative].
Then the functions $h_j=(\partial^{\beta_j}f_{i(j)})|_{T=0}$ are regular, vanish at $a$, and have invertible $y$-Jacobian at $a$. After one shrinking their zero scheme $C\subset B$ is smooth closed, has coordinates $w$, and at every $b\in C$, $L=\kappa(b)$, the substitution $y=\phi_b(W)+Y$ identifies its extended ideal with $(Y)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-residue-field]. The transformed generators retain their first exponents at $a$, ideal membership and generation. All their coefficients in $(Y,T)$ are regular on this same $C$, namely the restrictions of $\partial_y^\delta c_{i\gamma}/\delta!$. The old and new vertex derivatives lie in $(Z^\ell)$ and have invertible joint transverse Jacobian on $C$.
In addition suppose an $\mathcal O(B)$-linear operator $P$ on the $T$-series is given by finitely many coefficient extractions, full-series correction columns, and inverses of finite matrices with regular coefficients. Assume it projects onto the common kernel of the earlier tests, $P-1$ has image in the ideal of $f_1,\ldots,f_{s_{\ell-1}}$, it fixes all later $f_i$, and at $a$ preserves the first exponent of any series whose first monomial passes those tests. After the substitution, $P$ extends coefficientwise to an $\mathcal O(C)[[Y]]$-linear operator $P^-$ with all these properties for the earlier tests, including zero coefficients in every $Y$ degree. Every coefficient of its matrices, inverses and correction columns is regular on one common neighbourhood of $a$ in $C$. Empty old tests mean $P=1$; an empty newly essential block requires no equation.

source.place: BM 1997 Theorem 9.6, (9.7)--(9.8)(a)--(c), Remarks 9.9--9.11, pp.279--280; agent refinement transporting stored exact projections. Returned steps 1--4. ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 is the route reference; BM is read online, absent locally. No single Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Apply lem-trf-block-straightening-initial-jet for the equations and evaluated Jacobian entries. The Jacobian matrix is lower triangular. RingHom.map_det and Matrix.det_of_isLowerTriangular identify its determinant with the product of its nonzero diagonal entries, including the empty product for r=0.

Apply lem-trf-block-straightening-geometric-chart to the vanishing and nonzero determinant, obtaining the common affine chart, all geometric fields, and its Noetherian global ring. Copy these geometric fields into the full output.

For each stored operator use the coefficient-operator base-change theorem to transport its common-kernel projection. Enumerate the finite subset of earlier generator indices and apply hasIdealCorrection_map to the regular Y-series coefficient ring and to each pointwise formal coefficient ring; both are Noetherian. eval_map transports later-generator fixing. The transported kernel-image identity gives zero in every T and Y coefficient. The geometric chart residue surjection and center equality allow lem-trf-block-projection-first-transport to give the centered first-exponent clause. When old tests are empty every input is in the common kernel, so pointwise fixing proves both operators equal identity. Assemble all clauses into the unchanged output structure.

proof_origin.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), pp.279--280, (9.7)--(9.8), Remarks 9.9--9.11; stored-projection refinement recorded in the parent node. Read online 2026-10-26.; reduction into initial jets, a projection-free geometric chart, and first-exponent conjugacy. Generic projection transport and determinant computation are proved in Lean.
